questions.title: The General's Question
questions.storyContext: SAFTI briefing room. The Chief reads your summary, puts it down. "Commanders acted on 20-minute-old positions. The screen crashed at 500 users. Half the training area had no signal." He looks up: "Technology problem, design problem, or people problem?"
questions.facilitatorPrompt: What actually caused the stale data? The jungle network? A system that hid failure? Or commanders who never questioned the screen?

options.label: Network problem, sir. Dead zones stalled the data. Fund portable relays and satellite backup for every exercise.
options.consequence: The Chief nods slowly. "Radios have failed in every war ever fought. What's your plan for when these fail too?"

options.label: Design problem, sir. Stale data looked identical to fresh data. The screen should have warned instead of pretending.
options.consequence: "The screen lied by omission." The Chief writes that down word for word. Design reviews will never be the same.

options.label: People problem, sir. Commanders trusted the screen like a map. Train every officer to cross-check digital with radio and their own eyes.
options.consequence: A colonel at the back mutters, "Finally someone said it." The Chief pretends not to hear — and smiles.

options.label: Honestly sir, all three. Network, software, and training each failed. We have a phased three-year plan — it isn't cheap.
options.consequence: Silence. Then: "Expensive answers I can argue with. Honest ones I can fund." He keeps your report.

questions.title: The Next Generation
questions.storyContext: The Chief nods, then goes bigger: "The next generation of soldiers fights in a world as digital as it is physical. I can fast-track one capability into five years of SAF training. Every recruit will be shaped by it. Choose."
questions.facilitatorPrompt: What was the hardest thing we faced in Northstar — not just technically? Which capability would have changed the outcome?

options.label: Battlefield AI, sir — specialists deploying systems that learn from live data and suggest tactics in real time.
options.consequence: Five years on, an AI suggests a flanking route no human considered. The umpires check the rules twice. It's allowed.

options.label: Specialists fluent in both worlds, sir. Tech teams who understand terrain, commanders who understand data.
options.consequence: The first hybrid cohort graduates in three years. At their exercise, tech and terrain finally speak the same language.

options.label: Resilient communications, sir. Everything collapsed when the network dropped. Relays, satellites, radio drills — without comms, nothing else matters.
options.consequence: Next Northstar, the network drops for an hour — and nobody panics. The fallbacks click in like muscle memory.

options.label: Data literacy for every rank, sir. From private to general, everyone learns to read, question, and act on digital information.
options.consequence: Two years later, a corporal spots a sensor glitch a captain missed. The story becomes training-day legend.
